title: A coronary CT model retains diagnostic discrimination in sex subgroups
summary: A post-hoc analysis tested an existing coronary CT ischemia model against invasive pressure measurements in two cohorts. Vessel-level AUCs in women and men were 0.85 and 0.87 in CREDENCE and 0.81 and 0.86 in PACIFIC-1. These subgroup results do not establish equivalent performance, prospective clinical benefit or a newly developed model.
ai_technology: Convolutional coronary CT analysis and random-forest ischemia classifier
organization: Leiden University Medical Center; Amsterdam UMC

source_review.scope: Original full-text bibliographic date, relevant computational/statistical Methods and Results, bounded cohort and selection caveats; no operational clinical instructions.

evidence.tested: The previously developed classifier used quantitative plaque and stenosis features from neural image analysis; its random forest was trained in a separate 307-patient CREDENCE derivation cohort. This post-hoc study evaluated the 305-patient/868-vessel CREDENCE validation cohort and 208-patient/612-vessel PACIFIC-1 cohort. Sex-specific AUCs exceeded SPECT/MPI comparators; differences from PET in PACIFIC-1 were not significant.
evidence.unknown: Vessels are clustered within patients; subgroup tests were post hoc and do not establish equivalence or subgroup fairness. These are reused observational trial cohorts, not four independent samples or a new prospective deployment. Nonsignificant PET differences do not prove equivalence. Clinical outcomes and cost-effectiveness were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Existing neural segmentation/plaque quantification supplied features to a separately trained random forest for vessel-level ischemia prediction.
